reason: In free template outerNormal only `dir` (const short_t dir = s.direction()) is in scope; `!dim` names nothing (no namespace-scope dim in gismo at 6003fdf, md.dim is a member), so GCC rejects the non-dependent name.

evalAllDers_into maps tmp (d*mr x nc) as mr x nr instead of mr x nc; nr is the number of actives and nc the number of points, so when n>0 the mapped size is wrong (size mismatch or out-of-bounds write). The sibling Maps and the removed line use nc.

The shortcut unv(G) is renamed to inv(G). git grep -w unv at 05b6cad finds no caller, and the new free template does not clash with member .inv(). The public name is lost, but no in-tree code instantiates it.
Non-template constructor gsBoxTopology(short_t d, index_t n) calls addBox(m), but no `m` exists (members are m_dim, nboxes, m_boundary, m_interfaces, m_boxProp), so this is a hard compile error.
The posit overload of nextafter under #ifdef gsUniversal_ENABLED would return nextafter(y,y)==y. Its only call site, in gsKnotVector.hpp:957, is commented out, so the template is never instantiated.
In elementIndex the loop variable is `i`; m_bases[j] uses an undeclared non-dependent name (gsTensorBasis.h has no member j), which GCC rejects.
The new 4-argument matchWith forwards `bb`, which is only a local inside boundaryBasis; the parameter is `bi`. It is an undeclared non-dependent name, and no member bb exists.

_pattern::push takes row actives from the column space u instead of v, while still using rowMap = v.mapper(). For mixed spaces (v != u) the sparsity pattern gets wrong row indices. The in-tree caller poisson2_example uses u*u and is unaffected.

toBoxes uses `i = 2` instead of `i += 2`, so every element after the first overwrites columns 2-3. gsElementHelper::toBoxes is explicitly instantiated but never called: examples call gsHElementHelper::toBoxes.
In refine(gsMatrix) only k1 and k2 exist; _knotIndexToDiadicIndex(fLevel,b1) uses an undeclared `b1` (no member b1 in gsHTensorBasis.h) in an explicitly instantiated class, so it fails to compile.
getInclude has the parameter `id`; `in` is undeclared and non-dependent, gsFileData has no member `in`, and gsFileData<real_t> is explicitly instantiated.

updateBdr rebuilds m_masterBdr from bi.first() (the slave side) on the master geometry, but the constructor uses bi.second(). gsExprAssembler calls interfaceMap.updateBdr() in the moving-interface Jacobian loop, so the wrong boundary is used there.
`j` is only declared inside the earlier for-loop; in the ghost-knot branch gsGeometry<T>::degreeElevate(j, dir) uses an out-of-scope, undeclared name. The function parameter is `i`.
setBoxes assigns to `nBoxes`, which is the member function index_t nBoxes() const (the data member is nboxes). This is a hard error in a non-template class.

In gsMultiPatch::coefs(), `offset = coefsSize()` instead of `+=` makes every patch after the second write at the previous patch's size. Blocks overlap, the last rows stay zero and the assembled coefficient matrix is wrong.
In free template computeAuxiliaryData the local is `const int dir`; `jacT.row(!dim)` uses an undeclared name (dim is only a local of hessian_into, and there is no namespace-scope dim at a0fa869).

The macro now defines gsEigenSimplicialDLT, which matches the commit's own forward declaration. git grep finds no use of gsEigenSimplicialLLT, and the SimplicialLLT typedef points to gsEigenSimplicialLDLT either way, so behaviour does not change.

In asElementsUnrefine, k2's upper_bound range drops the +1 (domainUEnd() instead of domainUEnd()+1). A box ending at the domain end gets k2 one knot short, so the unrefinement box misses the last element. refine() and the removed line use +1.
In writeTexturedMesh the loop variable is `i`; params.col(j) uses an undeclared non-dependent `j` in an explicitly instantiated class, so it fails to compile.

constructInterfaceRep computes p1.iface(*it,p1) (patch with itself, p2 unused); the iface(const boundaryInterface&, const gsGeometry&) signature accepts it. git grep shows constructInterfaceRep is defined but never called.

m = n/2 is a declared const unsigned, so it compiles, but the Newton initial guess uses m+0.5 instead of n+0.5. For n=2 the start is x=0, where dpn=0 and the update divides by zero; in general the guess converges to wrong or duplicate roots. computeReference runs when lookup fails or digits != 0.
cNew is a scalar T member (gsMinimalResidual.h:105, cNew = a0/a1), so cNew.col(0) is invalid. gsMinimalResidual<real_t> is explicitly instantiated, so the build fails.

pruned(Scalar tol) passes `col` to scalar_prune_op. MatrixBase does not `using Base::col` (DenseBase is a dependent base), so `col` is an undeclared non-dependent name that GCC rejects at definition. pruned() itself has no dense caller in-tree.

`col` is not declared anywhere in gsDirichletValuesByL2Projection (only `com` = iter->unkComponent()); a non-dependent undeclared name fails at template definition in GCC. If it resolved, homogeneous BCs would get the wrong number of rows.

In the non-template gsBoxTopology::getBoundary(const patchSide& ps), `pc` is undeclared: it is not a member in gsBoxTopology.h, so the always-compiled .cpp breaks the build. getBoundary has no callers, so the runtime impact would be nil.

deriv2Single_into mixed-derivative row c gets an extra cwiseProduct(ev[l]) because r starts at l instead of l+1, so the result is wrong. The 0..k, k+1..l, l+1..d product pattern is visible in the hunk.

In blockTransposeInPlace's nr==colBlock branch, `i` is undeclared because it is only declared later in the else branch, so the build fails. Had it compiled, the wrong block would be transposed. The function is called from gsFunction.hpp:48 and gsTHBSplineBasis.hpp.

BiCGStab step overwrites the iterate (`x = alpha*y + w*z`) instead of accumulating it while the residual is still updated incrementally, so the solution is wrong. That is evident from the algorithm in the shown file.

The non-periodic consistency check drops the +1, so #coefs+deg+1==#knots no longer holds: it warns for every valid B-spline built from a knot vector and stays silent for bad ones. Only the diagnostic is affected, not the geometry. The removed line in the diff shows the +1.

In linearCombination_into's non-sameElement branch, `=` replaces `+=` inside the loop over active functions, so only the last basis function contributes. The sameElement branch and the removed line both use +=.

addInterface(index_t p1, boxSide s1, ...) uses `b1`, which is not declared in gsBoxTopology.h or the headers it includes. This is a non-template inline member included everywhere, so the build breaks. Intent-wise it is the wrong side.

`QLPiter = 1;` makes `if (QLPiter==1)` true on every step, so w/wl/wl2 are rescaled by gamma_QLP etc. and xl2 is rebuilt from x each iteration instead of only at the MINRES-to-QLP transition. That corrupts the iterates. The assign-then-compare tautology is visible.

computeReference sets x[0]=-1, then the plant overwrites it with 1e-12 (the mid-interval) instead of nudging it by +1e-12, so a quadrature node is wrong. The asymmetry with `x[n-1] -= 1e-12` is visible in the diff.

In gsMappedBasis::boundary, `i_const_iter` is used but only typedef'd later inside innerBoundaries (b_const_iter is declared on the line above), so the build fails. It would also be the wrong iterator type for m_topol.bBegin().
In initUniform, h=(last-first)/interior: the last interior knot coincides with `last`, the spacing is wrong, and interior=0 divides by zero. The removed line shows interior+1.

The coarse knot count uses the fine-level index fhigh[dim] on the coarse knot vector ckv instead of chigh, so size_of_coefs comes out wrong. Both are gsVector<index_t,d>. _updateSizeOfCoefs is called at lines 155 and 183. The fine line next to it uses the matching fkv/fhigh/flow.

update_structure resizes m_xmatrix to getMaxInsLevel() instead of +1, which drops the finest level's characteristic matrix and its active functions. needLevel(getMaxInsLevel()) and the needLevel body ('+1 for the initial basis') in the same hunk show that levels are 0-based and inclusive.

beginBdr's parameter is `bs`, but the plant writes GISMO_UNUSED(bi) (static_cast<void>(bi)), and bi is undeclared there. gsDomain.h is included by gsAssembler.h, gsExprAssembler.h and others, so the build breaks. The runtime semantics would be unchanged (the stub throws anyway).
In coarsening_direct, query4(row,upp,i) uses `row`, which is not declared in that scope (the sibling branch uses low,upp), so the build fails. The function is reached via gsHTensorBasis.hpp:1768.

matchWith takes bndOther from _other->boundaryOffset(bi.first().side(), ...), which is this patch's side rather than the neighbour's, so interface DOFs are matched wrongly. The removed line uses bi.second().

In _computePatternIfc (called from assembleIfc), the end iterator is basis1.domain()->endBdr(iFace.second().side()). It sets the end at numElementsBdr of the wrong side of patch1, so iteration skips elements or overruns when the sides have different element counts. beginBdr uses first().side().

getHNeighborhood uses level lvl-m instead of lvl-m+1 (the H-neighbourhood definition), giving a too-coarse support extension and a wrong admissible-refinement neighbourhood. It is reached from getNeighborhood for HB-splines via gsHElementMarker. The sibling getTNeighborhood (lvl-m+2) and the removed line show the convention.
BSplineCube overwrites the x column with x+0.5 instead of adding to the scaled coefficients, so all control points share one x coordinate and the cube is degenerate. The y and z lines use +=.

In the cv loop, `cIndex = atoi(unk->value())` comes before `int cIndex` is declared there, and no outer cIndex is in scope (the bc loop's is local), so the build fails. Intent-wise uIndex would never be read.
In uniformSplit, m_patches[mp] uses `mp` before `gsMultiPatch<T> mp(result)` is declared below, and there is no member `mp`, so the build fails. The loop variable is np.

splitAtMult starts at ubegin(), whose boundary knot has multiplicity p+1>=minMult, so it splits at the domain start and produces a degenerate piece. However, splitAtMult has no caller anywhere in the repo at this commit (git grep finds only its own declaration, definition and recursion).

GISMO_ASSERT(maxInteriorMultiplicity()<degree()) now rejects interior multiplicity p, which is legal and contradicts the message 'higher than p'. addLevel is called from nestedTHB_example and poissonTHB_example, so Debug builds throw; Release compiles the assert away.
getBasename's separator-only branch returns fn.substr(pos1), so the result keeps the leading '/' or '\'. The neighbouring code uses pos1+1 (the extension branch and getFilename).

The static non-template defaultOptions() only declares 'opt'. 'out' exists only as locals of toVTK, so out.addSwitch is an undeclared identifier and every TU including the header (gismo.h, gsParaviewDataSet.cpp) fails to compile.

boundaryOffset's loop variable is i; no j is declared in that function. The non-dependent name is a compile error wherever GISMO_ASSERT is active (Debug, gsDebug.h:89). Release expands GISMO_ASSERT to nothing (gsDebug.h:94) and builds.

coupling holds pair(k, localIndex), so .first is the patch number. localMappedIndex1 = coupling[i][j1].first puts the patch id in as a column of the jump matrix, while the j2 branch correctly uses .second.

`const bool fc = (0==fclose(fc));` passes the bool being declared to fclose(FILE*). There is no bool-to-FILE* conversion, and the expression is non-dependent, so the build breaks (fr is never closed either).

In asElements with m_manualLevels, _knotIndexToDiadicIndex(refLevel,j,k2) runs twice, so k2 is converted twice and k1 is never converted to the diadic index. The duplicate line is plainly visible; the types are the same as in the original k1 call.
gsGeometry<T>::degreeElevate(short_t const i, short_t const dir) has no j in scope. b->degreeElevate(j, dir) is an undeclared non-dependent name, and gsGeometry<real_t> is instantiated.
x.noalias() = *(m_transfers[i])*corr_local overwrites x on each subspace iteration, so the additive Schwarz apply returns only the last subspace correction instead of the sum.
BSplineCubeGrid offsets the x-center by ly instead of lx, which misplaces the cubes whenever lx != ly. The y argument also uses ly, so the copy/paste slip is visible in the diff.

reduceContinuity (overrides virtual gsBasis::reduceContinuity, so it is instantiated) now starts at ubegin() instead of ubegin()+1. It inserts the first boundary knot, and at levels >0 the step of 2 lands on old knots, against the comment 'skipping the first' / 'starting from 1'.

eval returns `_u.eval(k) > 0 ? _u.eval(k) : _w.eval(k)`. For the space-valued use at line 435 (ternary(m_eps - jac(G).det(), -derJacDet, space1*zeroVar)) _u yields a Scalar and _w an Eigen matrix with no implicit conversion between them. gsObjFoldoverFree<d,real_t>::gradObj_into is instantiated via gsBarrierCore<2/3,real_t>, so this fails to compile; in the scalar uses it would return the condition value. The commented original line shows _v.
gsEdge(v0,v1) initializes source(v1), target(v1), so every edge built by gsMesh::addEdge is degenerate. v0 is unused.

In gsTHBSplineBasis::active_into only low, upp, cur, currPoint, ind, maxLevel, temp_output, sz and p are declared. 'row' is undeclared, a non-dependent name error, and the class is explicitly instantiated. The intent is to convert 'low', which is used on the next line.
bb is a local of boundaryBasis, not of matchWith(const boundaryInterface & bi, ...). m_src->matchWith(bb, ...) names an undeclared identifier, and bi goes unused.
`for (k = m_offset[h]; k < m_offset[h]; ++k)` never executes, so assembleSystem adds no point contributions and the multipatch fit solves an empty system.
`gsMatrix<T> m_box1, m_box1;` redeclares the member m_box1, and m_box2 is no longer declared. Both errors occur in a class instantiated for real_t.
repairInterface refines patch bi.second().patch with refEltsFirst, which are element indices of the first patch. The first patch is never repaired and the second gets wrong elements.

uAdd does m_uit = a (ptrdiff_t). gsUKnotIterator has only a default ctor and an explicit ctor from knotVector&, so there is no conversion. uAdd is called in gsTensorBSplineBasis<1,T>::elementInSupportOf (gsBSplineBasis.hpp:68), which is instantiated, so the build fails; '+=' was intended.
addLine(v0,v1,midPts) places point i at start+i*h*step, so the first midpoint coincides with v0 (zero-length edge) and the last segment is twice as long. Called from gsMesh.hpp:107 and gsIOUtils.h.

swap() renames parrays_[spair.first] to name2 and then back to name1, so nothing is swapped and both entries are named wrongly relative to intent. Used via gsSurfMesh::swap_vertex_property in examples/cc_surf.cpp:331.
faceIndices(size_t i) looks up f->vertices[i], using the face index i instead of the loop index j. Every entry gets the same (or an out-of-range) vertex. Called from gsWriteOpenNurbs.hpp:287.

cf.pop_back() comes before `gsMatrix<T> cf(...)` is declared in the same function. The undeclared non-dependent name fails in the explicitly instantiated gsTensorBSpline. The intended removal of cv's doubled last point is also lost.
degreeIncrease(short_t const& i, short_t dir) has no `j` in scope, so tmp->degreeIncrease(j,dir) uses an undeclared name. It should pass the parameter i.

The basis is evaluated up to order m=domainDim() instead of the requested n, while evals[i] is read for i<=n. For gsMappedSpline<1,real_t> (instantiated in gsMappedSpline_.cpp) with n=2, evals[2] is out of bounds. For 2D and 3D the planted code only does extra work.
ins is std::pair<map::iterator,bool>, so ins.second->second applies -> to a bool. The virtual piece() is instantiated through gsFunction<T>::coord(), which builds a gsFuncCoordinate<T>.

The inner loop bound uses other.m_face[j] instead of m_face[i]. A copy of a mesh with fewer faces than vertices per face indexes past m_face, and faces with different vertex counts copy the wrong number of vertices.

step() pushes beta/alpha into m_delta, and the Lanczos diagonal needs 1/alpha added to it. Assigning 1/alpha discards the beta/alpha part, so the condition number is wrong when it is computed before convergence (m_error >= m_tol). The push_back(beta/alpha) is visible in the diff context.
out.dim.first is assigned twice (domainDim, then targetDim) and out.dim.second is never set. Consumers such as gsFuncData::eval reshape with dim.second, so they read a stale or wrong value.
With sorted=true the vertex is fetched with getVertex(i+1) but i is returned, an off-by-one. gsParametrization.h:378 calls findVertex(...,true).
locatePoints has no `it` in scope (the point is pt), so invertPoints(it, tmp, accuracy) uses an undeclared name. gsMultiPatch<real_t> is explicitly instantiated.
The parameter is dir. The primary gsTensorBasis<d,T> declares no `dim` (dim() comes from the dependent base and is only used as this->dim()), so unqualified `dim == -1` does not resolve.
operator-(typename E::Scalar const& s, _expr<E> const& v) has no `u`, so the undeclared non-dependent name is an error at template definition (GCC). It should pass v.
ElementBlocks[key].numElements = 1 overwrites the count instead of incrementing it (the comment says Increment), so a block with several elements reports 1 while actives and coefVectors keep growing.
The member is renamed to _u, but both constructors initialize _c(c), and eval/first/print use _c. The specialization is instantiated by operator*(Scalar, _expr<E2>) at mult_expr.h:252-265.

gsKnotVector (and its base gsDomain) has no second() at dc5c525, and gsPatchRule<real_t> is explicitly instantiated in gsPatchRule_.cpp. Semantically, knots(1)-knots(1) would give a zero lower length, as the symmetric upper line and the removed first() show.
The loop `k < m_offset[h]` starting at k = m_offset[h] never runs, so m_pointErrors stays empty. computeMaxNormErrors() is called from examples/gsMakeMultiPatch.cpp.
ab << t1, t1 collapses the interval [t1,t2] to a point, so the 1D gsPointGrid(t1,t2,n) returns n copies of t1.
boundaryBasis_impl declares bb (the uPtr) but uses bi.release(), and no `bi` is in scope in this function (bi is only a parameter of matchWith). The name is undeclared.

`std::vector<T> knots1, knots1;` redeclares a local, which is an error even in an uninstantiated function template. Apart from that, knots1 and knots2 are unused in isNested, so it changes no behavior.
sz = d*d/2 instead of d(d+1)/2 makes prm too small, and the loop that writes d(d+1)/2 entries would overflow it. But git grep finds no caller of the new static deriv2lex_inplace at 64b6eda.
result is initialized to {-1,0}, so `-1 == result[*it].second` is never true and anyPreImages returns all {-1,0}. It is used by gsMultiPatch.hpp:651.

getSpace(const gsFunctionSet<T>&, ...) accepts the mutable gsMultiPatch m_mp, so it compiles, but the FE space is built from the geometry instead of the basis m_mb, which does not match m_mapper. gsBarrierCore<2|3,real_t> instantiates gsObjFoldoverFree.

i is the box index (declared in the outer loop) and j is the direction, so _knotIndexToDiadicIndex(refLevel,i,maxKtIndexd) converts in the wrong direction, or indexes out of range when i>=d, whenever m_manualLevels is set.

outerNormal declares only `dir` (const short_t dir = s.direction()); bare `dim` is undeclared there (only md.dim exists), so `md.jacobian(k).col(!dim)` fails to compile; outerNormal is called from gsVisitorNeumann/Nitsche/Dg, so it is instantiated.

In evalAllDers_into the target Map t is built as mr x nr instead of mr x nc (nr = number of actives, nc = number of points), so `t = map.transpose()*s` (mr x nc) is assigned to a wrongly sized fixed Map: an Eigen assertion or out-of-bounds/garbled writes into tmp. The three sibling Maps all use nc.

The shortcut `unv(G)` (normalized normal) is renamed to `inv`; git grep -w unv at 05b6cad finds no caller and no conflicting free `inv` (only member .inv()), so nothing in the repo is affected, though the public name is now wrong and misleading.

The constructor gsBoxTopology(short_t d, index_t n) calls `addBox(m)`, but there is no `m` parameter or member (members are m_dim, nboxes, m_boundary, m_interfaces, m_boxProp). The class is not a template, so this is a hard error.

The posit overload of math::nextafter returns sw::universal::nextafter(y,y), which is just y, not the next value after x. Both arguments have the same type, so it compiles. The bug only takes effect in builds with gsUniversal_ENABLED.

In elementIndex the loop variable is `i`; `m_bases[j]` uses an undeclared non-dependent `j`, so GCC rejects it at definition. elementIndex is virtual in gsBasis (gsBasis.h:772), so it is instantiated anyway.

The new 4-arg matchWith passes `bb`, which is declared only as a local in boundaryBasis; the parameter is `bi`. The undeclared non-dependent name is an error, and the virtual matchWith (gsBasis.h:983) is instantiated with the class.

_pattern::push takes the row actives from the column space u (`u.source()...active`) while rd and rowMap come from v. For mixed or differing row/column spaces the interface sparsity pattern gets wrong or missing row entries. It is harmless only when u==v.

In gsElementHelper::toBoxes, `i = 2` instead of `i += 2` makes every box after the second overwrite columns 2-3, a real logic bug. But git grep at c99ef24 finds no caller of gsElementHelper::toBoxes: the examples call gsHElementHelper::toBoxes, which uses toBoxesAndLevels, and the class is only explicitly instantiated.

refine(gsMatrix const&) declares only `gsVector<index_t,d> k1, k2`; `_knotIndexToDiadicIndex(fLevel,b1)` uses an undeclared `b1` (b1 is a local of getBoxesAlongSlice). Even if it compiled, k1 would never be converted to dyadic indices.
getInclude's parameter is `id`; `(in!=-1)` in GISMO_ENSURE refers to an undeclared identifier, and git grep finds no namespace-scope `in`.

updateBdr sets m_masterBdr from m_masterGeom->boundary(bi.first()), the slave side, while the constructor uses bi.second(). updateBdr is called five times in gsExprAssembler.h, so closest-point projection uses the wrong boundary.
In degreeElevate(short_t const i, short_t const dir), `j` exists only inside the earlier for-loop, so `gsGeometry<T>::degreeElevate(j, dir)` uses an undeclared name in an instantiated member.
`nBoxes = n` assigns to the member function `index_t nBoxes() const` (shown in the context) instead of the data member `nboxes`. This is ill-formed in a non-template class.

In gsMultiPatch::coefs(), `offset = coefsSize()` instead of `+=` places patch k at the previous patch's size rather than the running sum. With 3 or more patches the blocks overlap and the rows near the end stay zero.
computeAuxiliaryData declares `const int dir` in the boundary branch, but `jacT.row(!dim)` uses an undeclared `dim`. There is no namespace-scope dim, and the function is instantiated via computeMap.

The planted line defines class gsEigenSimplicialDLT instead of gsEigenSimplicialLLT, which now matches the forward declaration. Nothing references either name: the typedef SimplicialLLT still aliases gsEigenSimplicialLDLT in both versions, so behavior is identical.

asElementsUnrefine now searches k2 with upper_bound over [domainUBegin, domainUEnd) instead of domainUEnd()+1. domainUEnd points at the last knot (gsKnotVector.h:54), so boxes ending at the domain end get k2 one too small. The function is called from gsAdaptiveMeshing and gsAdaptiveRefUtils.
writeTexturedMesh loops with `size_t i`; `params.col(j)` uses an undeclared `j`. gsParametrization is explicitly instantiated in gsParametrization_.cpp.

constructInterfaceRep builds the interface representation from `p1.iface(*it,p1)` instead of p2. The types match (iface(const boundaryInterface&, const gsGeometry&)), but git grep at 960ee6a finds no caller of constructInterfaceRep, and the base iface is GISMO_NO_IMPLEMENTATION.

The Newton initial guess uses cos(pi*(i+0.75)/(m+0.5)) with m = n/2 instead of n. The starting points become wrong for the degree-n Legendre polynomial, so Newton can converge to wrong or duplicate roots, giving wrong Gauss nodes and weights. The removed line shows n.

cNew is a scalar T (gsMinimalResidual.h:105, assigned `cNew = a0/a1` in the shown code), so `cNew.col(0)` is ill-formed once gsMinimalResidual<real_t> is explicitly instantiated in gsMinimalResidual_.cpp. The intended operand is vNew.

pruned(Scalar tol) passes `col` (DenseBase::col, from a dependent base, not visible to unqualified lookup) instead of `tol`. GCC and Clang reject the undeclared name at definition; lenient MSVC would defer the error. The dense MatrixBase::pruned has no caller at b5cc7e6 (only sparse .pruned in Eigen docs), so the bug never runs.
`col` is not declared in gsDirichletValuesByL2Projection (the component variable is `com`, used in the surrounding asserts); a non-dependent undeclared name in a template is a hard GCC error.
The parameter of the non-template gsBoxTopology::getBoundary(const patchSide& ps) is `ps`. gsBoxTopology.h has no member `pc`, so `m_boundary[i] == pc` uses an undeclared identifier.

In deriv2Single_into the mixed-derivative row is already multiplied by dev[l]. Starting at r=l multiplies it again by ev[l], so the result is wrong. The neighbouring loops skip k and l, which shows the pattern. gsTensorBasis is explicitly instantiated.

In blockTransposeInPlace's `nr == colBlock` branch only `j` is in scope (`i` is declared later, in the else branch), so `middleCols(i,colBlock)` names an undeclared non-dependent identifier inside the gsMatrix template.

`x.noalias() = m_alpha*m_y + m_w*m_z` overwrites the iterate with the update instead of adding it, while the residual is still decremented with `-=`. The solution is therefore wrong after the first step.

Dropping the +1 inverts the consistency check #coefs+deg+1==#knots: every valid non-periodic gsBSpline(KV,coefs) prints a spurious gsWarn, and off-by-one inputs are no longer reported. Only diagnostics change, not numbers. The removed line in the diff shows the +1.

In the per-point (sameElement=false, the default) branch of linearCombination_into, `=` instead of `+=` keeps only the last active function's contribution, so evaluation is wrong. The sameElement branch right above uses +=.

The inline addInterface(index_t p1, boxSide s1, index_t p2, boxSide s2, std::string l) has no `b1` in scope. In gsBoxTopology.h `b1` appears only as a parameter of findInterface, so patchSide(p1, b1) does not compile.

QLPiter is a member set to 0 in initIteration. With `+=` the `if (QLPiter == 1)` block runs only in the first step; with `= 1` it runs every step, resetting xl2 and rescaling w/wl/wl2 each iteration. gsMinResQLP<real_t> is instantiated. The always-true check is visible in the diff.

computeReference sets x[0] = -1, so `x[0] = 1e-12` moves the first node to ~0 instead of -1+1e-12, breaking the quadrature nodes. The appended function body shows x[0] = -1 and the symmetric `x[n-1] -= 1e-12`.

In gsMappedBasis::boundary only `b_const_iter` is typedef'd. `i_const_iter` is a local typedef of innerBoundaries (git grep finds no other declaration), so it is an undeclared non-dependent type name.

initUniform with h=(last-first)/interior puts the last interior knot at `last` (a duplicate end knot), stretches the ghost knots, and divides by zero when interior=0. The removed line in the diff shows /(interior+1).

cnmb_knts indexes the coarse knot vector ckv with fhigh (a fine-level index) instead of chigh. This gives a wrong coarse knot count and wrong size_of_coefs. The fine line below and the removed line both pair ckv with chigh.

update_structure calls needLevel(getMaxInsLevel()), which makes level index maxIns valid, so there are maxIns+1 levels. Resizing m_xmatrix to getMaxInsLevel() drops the finest level's active functions. The removed line resized to m_bases.size().
beginBdr's parameter is `bs`. GISMO_UNUSED(bi) expands to static_cast<void>(bi) with `bi` undeclared in the gsDomain<T> template. gsDomain.h is included by gsAssembler.h and others.

No variable `row` is in scope in this transfer function. Only `low`/`upp` are declared just above, and `row` occurs only as Eigen member calls. query4(row, upp, i) is therefore an undeclared identifier.

In gsTensorBasis::matchWith, bndOther takes the other patch's boundary on bi.first().side() instead of bi.second().side(). This matches the wrong DOFs across interfaces whenever the two sides differ. The removed line shows second().
In the interface assembly loop domIt starts at beginBdr(first side) but domItEnd = endBdr(second side), so the element range is mismatched. The begin/end pair is visibly inconsistent in the diff.

getHNeighborhood uses k = lvl - m + 1 (the H-neighbourhood level); `lvl - m` takes the support extension one level too coarse, so the neighbourhood is wrong for admissible marking. gsHElementHelper<2,3> is instantiated and getNeighborhood dispatches to it. The removed line shows +1.
BSplineCube(r,x,y,z): `C.col(0).array() = x + 0.5` overwrites all x-coordinates with a constant, which degenerates the cube. The y/z lines still use +=.

In the cv loop of gsXml<gsBoundaryConditions>::get_into, `cIndex = atoi(unk->value())` comes before `int cIndex = -1;`. The earlier cIndex belongs to the finished bc-loop scope, so this is an undeclared identifier.

In uniformSplit(index_t dir) the loop variable is `np`. `mp` is declared only after the loop (gsMultiPatch<T> mp(result)) and is not a member of gsMultiPatch/gsBoxTopology, so m_patches[mp] does not compile.

splitAtMult now iterates from ubegin(), the domain start knot of multiplicity p+1 >= minMult, so it calls splitAt at the boundary and pushes a degenerate piece; the loop already excludes the end knot via uend()-1. It is a public method of the explicitly instantiated class, but at this commit it has no caller in the repo besides its own recursion.

GISMO_ASSERT(maxInteriorMultiplicity()<degree()) rejects valid multiplicity p (and every degree-1 basis with interior knots) in debug builds; addLevel is used by poissonTHB_example --manual and nestedTHB_example. The message 'higher than p' contradicts the condition.
name = fn.substr(pos1) keeps the separator, so getBasename("dir/foo") returns "/foo". The other branch and getFilename both use pos1+1.

In static defaultOptions() only gsOptionList opt is declared; the only 'out' in the file is a local in other functions, so out.addSwitch is an undeclared identifier (and the makeSubfolder option would be missing).

boundaryOffset has only loop variable i, so m_bases[j] is undeclared in debug builds, where GISMO_ASSERT expands to code (gsDebug.h); in release the assert is empty. At run time it would only change an assert message.
localMappedIndex1 = coupling[i][j1].first takes the patch index (patch1 is the line above) instead of the local dof .second, so jump matrices get wrong column indices; the j2 line uses .second.
fclose(fc) passes the const bool being initialized instead of FILE* fr; bool does not convert to FILE*, and the file would not be closed.
_knotIndexToDiadicIndex(level, dir, index_t& knotIndex) converts in place; with two calls on k2, k2 is converted twice and k1 never when m_manualLevels (addLevel path used in poissonTHB_example).

degreeElevate(short_t const i, short_t const dir) has no 'j'; the non-dependent undeclared name fails, and gsGeometry<real_t> is instantiated (the method is virtual). The removed dir==-1/error branches are dropped too.
x is setZero'd and should accumulate the corrections of all subspaces; 'x.noalias() =' keeps only the last one. m_transfers holds pointers (moveToPtr), so *(m_transfers[i]) is valid.
The x-offset of BSplineCube uses ly instead of lx, so the grid is misplaced whenever lx != ly. BSplineCubeGrid is a public creator exposed in the pybind (gsNurbsCreator_.cpp).

The loop starts at ubegin() instead of ubegin()+1, inserting a knot at the boundary knot and, for lvl>0 with step 2, hitting old rather than new knots; this contradicts the comment 'skipping the first'. reduceContinuity is used in poissonTHB_example and stokes_ieti_example.

eval returns _u.eval(k) (the condition) instead of _v.eval(k). In gsObjFoldoverFree::gradObj_into (virtual, instantiated at line 323), ternary(m_eps - det, -derJacDet, space1*zeroVar) mixes a scalar with a matrix in ?:, and gsMatrix has no scalar constructor. The scalar uses (chi) would return eps-det. The commented line above shows _v.
gsEdge(v0,v1) initializes source(v1), so source==target and v0 is lost for every edge built by gsMesh::addEdge (sharp is a declared member).
active_into has no 'row' (locals are low, upp, cur), so the non-dependent undeclared argument fails. The overload _knotIndexToDiadicIndex(level, gsVector<index_t,d>&) expects the point 'low'.
'bb' is a local of boundaryBasis, not in scope in matchWith (parameter bi), so it is an undeclared identifier.
k < m_offset[h] is never true, so assembleSystem (called at gsFitting.hpp:94 for mapped fitting) assembles nothing and the system stays empty.

'gsMatrix<T> m_box1, m_box1;' redeclares a member, an error in the template definition. m_box2, used in gsAffineFunction.hpp (ctor and clamping), disappears; the duplicate itself is visible in the diff.

refEltsFirst (elements of the first patch from repairInterfaceFindElements) is refined on bi.second().patch, so the second patch is refined with the wrong element list and the first never; the removed code used first().

m_uit is gsUKnotIterator<T>, which has no constructor or assignment from difference_type (only default and an explicit KV ctor). uAdd is instantiated via gsBSplineBasis.hpp:68 elementInSupportOf, and the method is meant to advance relatively.
With h = len/(midPts+1) and i starting at 0, the first midpoint coincides with v0 and the last gap is 2h. addLine(v0,v1,midPts) is used in gsMesh.hpp:107 and gsIOUtils.h.
Both renames hit parrays_[spair.first] (name2 then back to name1), so swap is a no-op; it is called by gsSurfMesh::swap_vertex_property, which examples/cc_surf.cpp uses.
f->vertices[i] uses the face index parameter i instead of loop index j, giving a wrong or out-of-bounds vertex. faceIndices is called in extensions/gsOpennurbs/gsWriteOpenNurbs.hpp:287.

`cf.pop_back()` uses `cf` one line before `gsMatrix<T> cf(...)` is declared, so GCC rejects the non-dependent name at definition. gsMatrix also has no pop_back, and the list `cv` keeps its doubled last point.
`tmp->degreeIncrease(j,dir)` in degreeIncrease(short_t const& i, short_t dir): `j` is not declared anywhere in scope, so the non-dependent name is a compile error.

m = domainDim() is passed instead of the derivative order n to gsMappedBasis::evalAllDers_into(index_t patch, const gsMatrix&, index_t n, vector&, bool). For gsMappedSpline<1,real_t> (instantiated in gsMappedSpline_.cpp) with n=2, evals has only 2 entries and evals[2] is out of bounds.
`ins` is pair<map::iterator,bool>, so `ins.second->second` applies -> to a bool. The virtual piece() is instantiated through gsFunction<T>::coord(), which constructs gsFuncCoordinate<T>.

The inner bound uses `other.m_face[j]->vertices.size()` (face j) instead of face i. With a single triangle, m_face[1] is read out of bounds; with mixed tri/quad faces the copy loop uses the wrong vertex count.

getConditionNumber before convergence replaces the last Lanczos diagonal with 1/alpha instead of adding it (step() does `m_delta.back()+=(1./alpha)`), so the condition number is wrong. The += in step() is not in the shown context, only the save/restore hints at it.
compute() assigns out.dim.first twice (domainDim, then targetDim), so dim.first is wrong and dim.second is never set. gsFuncData::eval() reshapes with dim.second, so the results are wrong.
In sorted mode the loop uses getVertex(i+1) (1-based), but the function now returns i, one less. gsParametrization.h:378 calls findVertex(...,true) and gets off-by-one vertex indices.
`invertPoints(it, tmp, accuracy)`: no `it` is declared in locatePoints (the point is `pt`), so the non-dependent undeclared name is a compile error.

`if (dim == -1)` in degreeReduce: gsTensorBasis declares no `dim` member (only loop locals and the base's dim() via this->), so unqualified lookup fails. Even if the base's dim() were found, a member function compared to int is ill-formed.
operator-(Scalar s, _expr<E> const& v) returns sub_expr<...>(_expr(s), u), but `u` is not a parameter of this function, so the non-dependent name fails at definition. The variable meant is v.

`ElementBlocks[key].numElements = 1` resets the count, which the comment says should be incremented, so every block reports 1 element while actives/coefVectors keep growing. gsMultiPatch.hpp's twin uses `+= 1`.

The member is renamed to `_u`, but the constructors still initialize `_c(c)` and eval()/first()/print() still use `_c`. This specialization is instantiated by scalar*expr (operator* at mult_expr.h:252-298), which is used everywhere.

gsKnotVector at dc5c525 has first()/last() but no second(), so `knots.second()` fails when gsPatchRule<real_t> is instantiated (CLASS_TEMPLATE_INST in gsPatchRule_.cpp). Seeing this needs the gsKnotVector API.
`k < m_offset[h]` starting at k = m_offset[h] never runs, so computeMaxNormErrors computes no point errors and leaves m_max_error/m_min_error unset.
`ab << t1, t1` makes the interval [t1,t1], so the 1D gsPointGrid(t1,t2,n) returns n copies of t1 and ignores t2.
boundaryBasis_impl calls `bi.release()`, but only `bb` (the uPtr) is declared there (`bi` is a parameter of matchWith), so the non-dependent undeclared name is a compile error.

`std::vector<T> knots1, knots1;` redeclares a local in the same scope, which GCC diagnoses at template definition in a header included everywhere. At runtime it would be harmless, since knots1/knots2 are unused.

sz = d*d/2 instead of d*(d+1)/2 would size prm too small (for d=2, prm has 2 entries but 3 are written: out of bounds). But deriv2lex_inplace has no caller at 64b6eda (git grep finds only its definition).
result is initialized to {-1,0}, so `-1 == result[*it].second` is never true and no preimage is ever stored. anyPreImages is used in gsMultiPatch.hpp:651.

getSpace(const gsFunctionSet<T>&, index_t) accepts the gsMultiPatch m_mp, so it compiles. But the FE space then uses the geometry instead of the basis m_mb (which the removed line and the sibling functions use), so the gradient space and mapper do not match.

In asElementsUnrefine with m_manualLevels, maxKtIndexd is converted with direction i (the box index) instead of j. _knotIndexToDiadicIndex(level, index_t dir, index_t&) then reads the wrong direction, or an invalid one when i >= d, and k2 is clamped wrongly.
